_comment: THIRD-PARTY VENDORED SOURCE, CUT DOWN. This directory is upstream release
v1.1.1 of cuchi_computer with most of it removed: what is left is the desktop
shell and its window manager. Every file kept is byte-identical to `git
archive` of the tag named in `commit` outside its BR-PATCH blocks, every file
removed is listed under `removed`, and every file that did not come from
upstream is listed under `added`. So the next upstream bump is: extract the
new tag beside this directory, delete what `removed` names, re-apply the
tools/verify.sh reads this file. The `vendored third-party` gate checks that
the LICENSE is present, that every BR-PATCH marker in the tree is declared
here and every patch declared here is present in the tree, and that
tools/deploy.sh actually syncs this resource to the box -- because shipping
a resource that never reaches the server is a failure mode this project has
THIS RESOURCE DOES NOTHING ON ITS OWN. It has no server half, no command and
no keybind. br_core opens it, feeds it and closes it; the contract is
docs/terminals.md, and client/shell.lua's header is the Lua half of it.
why_this_pin: v1.1.1 is the latest release. main has one commit after it, 604df68
that loads google.com in an iframe. It is not taken -- nothing here browses
the web -- but it is where the size of this copy's one window came from.
license_note: GNU General Public License v3.0, the notice upstream ships at its root and
kept here unmodified. The GPL lets this copy be modified and distributed as
long as the source travels with it and the changes are marked, which this
repository does by being public, by the BR-PATCH notes in the files, and by
this file (dated, under `vendored_on`). The added files below are part of
this modified copy and are under the same licence.
The terminal app that runs inside this desktop is ours: its source is
ui-src/terminal in this public repository, its build output is committed
under nui/apps/terminal/ so it ships with the resource, and it talks to the
desktop only by postMessage. If its terms ever needed to differ from the
GPL's, serving that output from a resource of its own is the clean line.
This is a record of what was done, not a lawyer's opinion.
The two font files in nui/fonts/ are a second, separate licence: the Ubuntu
Font Licence 1.0, whose text travels beside them (see `added`).

provenance_check.claim: Of the 53 files at v1.1.1, 6 are here with the SAME GIT BLOB ID as the tag: LICENSE, README.md, locales/main.js and nui/assets/images/{error,exit,info}.png at their own paths. 6 more are here with BR-PATCH blocks (see `patches`). The other 41 are removed (see `removed`) -- console.png among them since 2026-10-05: it was here renamed to terminal.png as the app's placeholder icon, and the owner's round-2 icon (our own nui/assets/images/terminal.svg) replaced it.
how: for f in LICENSE README.md locales/main.js nui/assets/images/error.png nui/assets/images/exit.png nui/assets/images/info.png; do
provenance_check.note: Compare BLOB IDS, not worktree files, and extract with `git -c core.autocrlf=false archive v1.1.1`. Upstream's blobs are LF; a Windows clone with core.autocrlf=true hands out CRLF, which is about the clone and not about the code.

why_vendored: Owner, 2026-10-04 (#396): Season 2 terminals run a Cloudscape app 'inside a
modified cuchi_computer'. Upstream needs ESX or QBCore plus oxmysql and this
gamemode runs neither, so the modified copy keeps the desktop and drops the
framework, the database and the roleplay apps. Vendored rather than
installed by hand for the reason every third-party resource here is:
tools/deploy.sh ships what is in this repository and nothing else.

replaced_by_our_own_icon: nui/assets/images/console.png -- here as nui/assets/images/terminal.png (the app's placeholder icon) until 2026-10-05, when the owner named the app Control Tower and gave its icon; nui/assets/images/terminal.svg, an original drawing, took its place (see `added`)
removed.why_the_sounds_went: boot.mp3 played on every opening and message.mp3 on every message box. This project's sounds are each the owner's pick (br_lib/config/audio.lua) and these two never were, so they went with the rest; nothing else here ever played a sound. The 'look' the owner chose this resource for is the desktop, which is all still here.

added.client/shell.lua: the whole Lua half: open (with the copy block, the function catalog -- its page-load range included, round 3 -- and the desktop's boot range and game time), update, result, the game clock (Clock) and close for br_core, NUI focus, and the page's callbacks -- a run's function id and its options shape-checked on the way through, and a run's last word the app never showed handed back to br_core for a toast (only a toast this shell relayed, once), and the storm's close (round 4): br_core's 'offline' close tells the page to play its blue screen and power-off and holds the focus vote until the page says the screen is dark (`off`), 4 s at most, or until anything else needs the computer; and the map pick (round 4, owner 2026-10-06): the app's 'Set location' passed to br_core, Hide (the page out of sight, the focus let go) and Show (back, with the spot picked, shape-checked), and a run's spot shape-checked like its options. Its header is the contract's Lua side.
added.nui/br.js: the page's bridge: br_core's messages in (the catalog on open, the state alone on each once-a-second update, the game's time on each new minute), the terminal app's requests out (a run's options shape-checked), Escape (the boot included), a boot of a random length in br_core's range that ends on the desktop, the app launched from its desktop icon (loaded then, unloaded by its window's close), a run's last word held for an app that is away or still loading and handed back for a toast if the computer closes first, the window's eight resize handles and its maximize, a drag fix for windows that hold an iframe, and the tab's loading symbol (owner, 2026-10-06, round 3): the app says a page load started or ended, and the tab wears br.css's .br-loading for exactly that long -- taken off when the page shows, when the app or the computer goes away, and by a backstop at the load's length plus a second (15 s at most). And round 4 (owner, 2026-10-06): the storm's close -- the computer shut at once, then a Windows-style blue screen in the copy block's words for 1.5 s and a CRT power-off for 0.6 s, the screen then removed from the page and the shell told (`off`); and the tab's loading symbol from the app's icon click, through its first page's white load, until the app says that page showed (15 s at most); and the map pick (round 4): the app's 'Set location' passed on, the page hidden and shown again around the big map, the app's frame given the keyboard back, and what was picked handed to the app.
added.nui/br.css: the Ubuntu face from nui/fonts/, the desktop's wallpaper (owner, 2026-10-05), and the terminal window as a web browser's frame (owner, 2026-10-05): upstream's title bar restyled into a tab strip with one tab (the app's icon and title) and drawn window controls (minimize, maximize, close), one look whatever the app's light/dark mode (round 2); the resize handles and their cursors; the taskbar's date hidden; and the tab's loading symbol (round 3), a turning ring in place of the app's icon under .br-loading, removed with its class (#385); and the storm's close (round 4): a black screen holding a Windows-style blue screen, whose CRT power-off under .br-crt -- the file's one other animation -- runs once, on an element br.js removes when it ends. The browser's toolbar (back, forward, reload, the address bar) is the app's own, since it walks the app's navigation.
added.nui/assets/images/wallpaper.webp: the desktop's wallpaper (owner, 2026-10-06, round 5: 'Please use this graphic as the new wallpaper for the computers.'): his own in-game screenshot of the Vinewood sign by day, over the hills, 2000x1125 WebP, 341370 bytes, sha256 6452b54eb45303b6cd6850ad879d25f878510c247d0b6f33911dc2fba137c960. It replaced his night-time one of 2026-10-05 (1501x845). nui/br.css draws it over the desktop's upstream color.
added.nui/assets/images/terminal.svg: the Control Tower icon (owner, 2026-10-05, round 2: 'use the attached icon'): an ORIGINAL drawing made for this project in the spirit of the owner's reference -- a tall shaft, a glazed cab with mullions over a railed deck, roof antennas -- a white tower on a blue tile. The desktop icon, the taskbar, the window's tab and the app's top bar. Not upstream's, not the reference image.
added.nui/fonts/LICENSE-UFL-1.0.txt: that package's LICENSE, the Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0, verbatim (sha256 52fdffecb23a020de527f68c516cac16dbbaf2dbb73fd9e29e2149703b881c82)
added.nui/apps/terminal/: BUILD OUTPUT, NOT SOURCE: the Season 2 terminal app (React + Cloudscape), written here by ui-src's `npm run build` (vite.terminal.config.ts) from ui-src/terminal, and byte-compared with a fresh build by `npm run build:check` in CI. Never edit it by hand; rebuild. It holds no BR-PATCH marker and must not. Since round 4 it also carries the Volts face: assets/anton-latin-400-normal.woff2, @fontsource/anton 5.3.0's files/anton-latin-400-normal.woff2 byte for byte (sha256 d0fa07ff63dd60cbc0e2f58e29c802dca2a5ae0276c999f59c6111ab7bbaec3b, the file br_ui ships), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, whose text is beside it as assets/LICENSE-OFL-1.1-anton.txt (that package's LICENSE, verbatim; sha256 9267baca92b7a7ce9db6dd9e6cc32c9fe3ddf1ac96e421d5f87c5746b9089d6a).

patches.what: One client script, client/shell.lua; no shared or server scripts, no oxmysql; the English locale only. The header fields (version, name, author, repository) are upstream's.
patches.why: Standalone: no framework and no database exist on this server, and br_core drives the desktop.
patches.upstream_fixable: no -- upstream is a framework resource by design

patches.what: Adds br.css and br.js; removes the language picker, the four non-English locale scripts and commands.js.
patches.why: One locale and one app, and the bridge to client/shell.lua.

patches.what: Removed the @import of Ubuntu from fonts.googleapis.com. br.css declares the same two weights from nui/fonts/.
patches.why: NUI pages load at join on every client, so the import was a request to Google from every player on every join, whether or not they ever used a computer -- and no Ubuntu at all for a client that could not reach it. The rest of this project ships its fonts (ui-src's @fontsource imports).
patches.upstream_fixable: yes -- shipping the font is an ordinary upstream change

patches.what: Removed the removed apps' rules. Every rule for the desktop, the taskbar, the loader, windows and message boxes is untouched.
patches.why: The apps they styled are gone.

patches.what: One app, `terminal`: a window whose body is an iframe (#terminal-frame), 1440x880 (a browser window; br.css caps it at 98vw x 92vh until the player resizes it), with a maximize button in its title bar and eight resize handles (round 2), and `icon`, the app's own icon file. Upstream's seven apps are gone.
patches.why: The terminal app is a React + Cloudscape page with its own document, so Cloudscape's global styles cannot restyle the desktop around it. The size is a browser's because the owner asked for the window to look like one (2026-10-05) and the app's side navigation and cards need the room; upstream's own iframe app was 960x630. Round 2: 'We should also have the ability to resize (when grabbing the edges) and maximize the window.'

patches.what: Removed the console history, the roleplay state (fake IP, identifier, mail account) and upstream's message handler (show, version, identifier, force-close). br.js handles every message now.
patches.why: The handler booted the desktop from a framework callback's data. Here br_core's payload boots it.

patches.symbol: DOMContentLoaded: SetLocale, the picker, the saved theme
patches.what: Removed the language picker's wiring and the theme restored from localStorage. The desktop always opens in style.css's own colors.
patches.why: NUI localStorage belongs to the resource NAME on the player's machine, not to this server, so a theme or a locale chosen in cuchi_computer on any other server would have followed the player here -- and a locale this copy no longer ships throws every second. br.js pins the locale to English for the same reason.

patches.what: The taskbar's power button closes at once through br.js, instead of a confirmation box and a 1.5 s 'shutting down' screen.
patches.why: The player is standing in a live match and the keyboard is the desktop's until it closes. Escape closes the same way.
patches.upstream_fixable: no -- the confirmation is a choice for a roleplay server

patches.symbol: DOMContentLoaded: the mail and market blocks
patches.what: Removed. Each began by reading Applications.mail / Applications.market, which no longer exist and would have thrown.

patches.symbol: OnConsoleCommand, AddConsoleLine, ClearConsole, AddInformation, setupMail, refreshMails
patches.what: Removed. OpenApp and FocusApp still carry branches for the console and mail app ids; nothing opens those ids, so the branches never run, and they are left as upstream wrote them.

patches.symbol: DOMContentLoaded: the desktop icon's ; OpenApp: the taskbar icon's
patches.what: An app's own `icon` (Applications[app].icon) when it names one, else upstream's assets/images/<appName>.png.
patches.why: The app's icon is an SVG drawing (Control Tower, owner 2026-10-05 round 2), and upstream builds a .png path from the app id in both places.
patches.upstream_fixable: yes -- an icon field per app is an ordinary upstream change

patches.what: Removed. br.js writes the taskbar's hour and minute from the GAME's clock (br_core sends it on each new minute while the computer is open), and the date is not shown.
patches.why: Owner, 2026-10-05 round 2: 'Can you make the computer clock match the game clock?' Upstream wrote the player's own clock and date every second.
patches.upstream_fixable: no -- a game clock is this server's

patches.what: One key left, date_format (the taskbar clock's). Every line of text the desktop shows is br_core's, from the copy block in br_lib/config/terminals.lua.
patches.why: The owner writes or approves every player-facing line, in one place (#396).

untouched_on_purpose: The window manager in script.js -- Load, OpenApp, CloseApp, FocusApp, MinimizeApp, MakeElementDraggable, MessageBox, ShutdownComputer, editTheme -- is upstream's, byte for byte, but for BR-PATCH 12's icon path in OpenApp. br.js calls it; resizing and maximizing are br.js's own, beside it.
style.css's desktop, taskbar, loader, window and message-box rules, and its :root colors (upstream's first theme), which are the look the owner chose this resource for.
The taskbar's markup (#hours, #date) and the en-US date_format the clock is written in; since round 2 the time is the game's (BR-PATCH 13) and #date is hidden by br.css.
ShutdownComputer and MessageBox stay although nothing calls them now: they are the window manager's, and a later app may want a message box.
